title: Conversations & Review
description: Put everything together with full conversational dialogues and a comprehensive review of all lessons.

exercises.prompt: Arrange a greeting conversation: 'Hello, how are you? I am fine, thank you.'
exercises.explanation: A typical Tamil greeting exchange: vanakkam (hello), eppadi irukkeenga (how are you), naan nallaa irukkein (I am fine), nandri (thank you).

exercises.prompt: Hello, my name is Anitha. I want coffee please.
exercises.correct: vanakkam, en peyar Anitha. enakku kaapi venum thayavu seidhu.
acceptedVariants: vanakkam en peyar Anitha enakku kaapi venum thayavu seidhu
vanakkam, en peyar anitha. enakku kaapi venum thayavu seidhu.
exercises.explanation: This combines greetings, introductions, and making a request with 'venum' and 'thayavu seidhu'.
exercises.hint: sounds like: vanakkam, en peyar Anitha. enakku kaapi venum thayavu seidhu.

exercises.explanation: 'Eppadi irukkeenga?' means 'How are you?'. This is a natural follow-up after introducing yourself.
These sentences combine vocabulary and grammar from multiple lessons into practical phrases.

exercises.question: You are at a restaurant. How do you say 'I want food, please'?
exercises.explanation: 'Enakku saappaadu venum thayavu seidhu' politely says 'I want food, please' using the dative + venum pattern.
'Poitu varein' means goodbye (literally 'I will go and come back') and is pronounced 'poy-tu vuh-rain'.
'Kadai enga irukku?' combines the place word 'kadai' (shop) with the question pattern 'enga irukku' (where is it).

exercises.prompt: Arrange to say 'I like fruits, I don't want coffee':
exercises.explanation: 'Enakku pazhangal pidikkum, enakku kaapi venaam' = I like fruits, I don't want coffee. 'Venaam' is the negative of 'venum'.
